children: Markets may be underestimating the scale of the global tightening cycle as commodity prices rise, financial conditions remain accommodative, and central banks show a more hawkish reaction to inflation, according to Deutsche Bank.
Inflation risks could keep pressure on central banks

The Federal Reserve, European Central Bank, and Bank of Japan have all raised rates in the past two weeks, marking a return to a globally synchronized hiking cycle, Deutsche Bank macro strategist Henry Allen said.

Allen said central banks were already responding more aggressively after the 2021-23 inflation episode, when policymakers were considered having reacted too slowly. Unlike in 2022, when the Fed and ECB began hiking with inflation above 8%, they have started the current cycle with inflation at less than half those levels.

September's commodity gains, particularly in oil and gas, have yet to be fully reflected in inflation data and surveys, which mostly run through August. Brent crude was around $102 a barrel after a pullback lately but remained above its levels throughout August, the note said.

Deutsche Bank also said policymakers may have less tolerance for another prolonged inflation overshoot after inflation remained above target for several years. The note cited Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's observation that inflation had been running above target for “more than five years.”

Financial conditions are more accommodative than when the Fed began hiking in 2022, with the S&P 500 within 2% of its record high versus a correction of more than 10% at the start of the previous cycle. U.S. high-yield spreads are around 270 basis points today, compared with more than 400 basis points in 2022, according to the note.

Deutsche Bank said markets have historically tended to underestimate the scale of hiking cycles at the beginning. In 2022, investors initially priced about 200 basis points of Fed hikes in the first year, while the Fed ultimately delivered more than 400 basis points.

That compares with current pricing of at least 100 basis points of Fed hikes and more than 125 basis points of ECB tightening in total, including the 50 basis points already delivered. The STOXX 600 remains just over 3% below its record, the note said.

Deutsche Bank said the resilience of risk assets actually points to the risk of a more hawkish tightening cycle. Growth resilience since the Iran conflict began has helped give central banks space to hike, the note said.
If earnings remain strong and AI continues to boost productivity and growth, equities may not be significantly affected by higher rates.

title: Deutsche Bank says markets may be underpricing rate hikes
